HCBCOGN312.name: Psycholinguistics
HCBCOGN312.contribution: examines speech production/comprehension, aphasia and dyslexia with experimental language neuroscience, providing a specific cognitive-function and impairment strand within the physical/mental-health concept
HCBCOGN312.topics: Psycholinguistics is the study of the neurobiological and psychological factors that enable us to acquire, use, and understand language. Modern research draws on cognitive psychology, neuroscience, and computer science to investigate how language is processed. The course focuses primarily, though not exclusively, on the neuroscience of language. Students examine theoretical and experimental issues in speech production and comprehension, language impairments, the relationship between thought and language, and the evolution and acquisition of language. They also gain hands-on experience with experimental approaches to the study of language and develop an understanding of human linguistic capacity as a subject of multidisciplinary research. Topics covered: What is language? Evolutionary aspects of language and animal communication; language and thought; aphasia; language acquisition; bilingualism; speech comprehension; semantics; reading and dyslexia; speech production.

candidateDecisions.label: Physical and mental health through psychology and cognitive science

analysis: The two options are qualified science comparisons. The first provides molecular and systems foundations through genetics, pathology, physiology, infection, drug action and laboratory investigation. Mechanisms of Disease analyses organ-system cases, including evidence relevant to diagnosis and treatment, within academic course work. The second concentrates on cognitive and perceptual processes, psychopathology, psychosocial health, qualitative experience and persuasion, with physiological and pharmacological foundations retained. Perception and Action and Psycholinguistics contribute evidence on sensory processing and language impairment. Persuasive Communication contributes framing and persuasion methods rather than clinical communication. Health Psychology covers consultation and shared decisions academically. Both routes study evidence synthesis, quantitative analysis and ethical judgment. The six-course difference each way implements the contrast between molecular and laboratory investigation and cognitive and social health. Public health and ethics contribute to both without a further distinct generator. No UCR option implements the integrated practical or workplace medical sequence. Partial alignment pairs brain and behaviour with the combined nervous-system and mental-health block and anatomy with the urogenital content. Clinical reasoning and workplace learning remain separate. UCR research is optional and additional.

alignment.rationale: Both address biological foundations of health and disease. UCR focuses on cells, metabolism and genetics.
UCR Human Physiology studies circulation and breathing. Utrecht connects those systems to symptoms and clinical reasoning.
UCR Biochemistry studies metabolism at the molecular level. Utrecht also integrates digestive-system medicine.
UCR Pharmacology studies drug action, kinetics and adverse effects. Utrecht places drug treatment within the medical curriculum.
